result:
`index.html` is written to the working directory and passes the skill's full verify pipeline (contract checks, doctor ≥85, and desktop/mobile/reduced-motion/no-JS browser evidence).

The design builds one bespoke visual system for Ferrymead Bakehouse rather than forcing a named archetype: a warm flour-cream ground, a single muted estuary-teal accent, and a serif display paired with a system sans for body/UI (all system font stacks, since no web fonts are allowed). The signature moment is the tagline made literal — a wavy tide-line motif opens low in the hero (a "low tide" state, with the ferry hall's silhouette drawn in flat CSS/SVG shapes behind the title) and reappears as a rising tide divider before the closing CTA, so the water bookends the page the way "Bread on the tide" bookends the copy. Motion stays restrained and unhurried per the brief: soft one-shot entrance reveals (transform/opacity only, IntersectionObserver-driven), a slow horizontal wave drift in the hero, and a small contained parallax on the tide divider — no pinning, no scroll-jacking, and everything freezes to a fully visible static state under `prefers-reduced-motion` or with JavaScript disabled. The four loaves get simple hand-drawn SVG icons (slashed country loaf, dark rye with caraway flecks, salt-crystal crust, stacked crumpet rings) instead of photos, the subscription steps and hall history are broken into scannable list/timeline units using only the verbatim copy, and the layout uses fluid clamp() type and auto-fit grids so it holds up cleanly from 390px to 1440px with no overflow or clipping.
